message:
Integrated touch works end to end because each hand over matches in kind and in place. Plain words: soft skin squeezes two films on the hard bone, slow squeeze goes through the touch chip and fast shake goes direct to the tiny computer, and both leave together as one safe message. The stack from outside is ridged skin over gel under 2.50 mm total in the GelSight High-Resolution Robot Tactile Sensors (E2) over Polyvinylidene Fluoride, where Polyvinylidene Fluoride means PVDF vibration film, over capacitive taxels on flat facets in the compound-eye drape sketch (E65) with flex at 3.18 mm bend in the BioTac Product Manual (E43) to the on-finger board, where Capacitance-to-Digital Converter means CDC and Microcontroller Unit means MCU and Serial Peripheral Interface means SPI and Analog-to-Digital Converter means ADC, so static force via 9.00 ms CDC update in the AD7147A Rev B (E41) and vibration via 1 Msps ADC in the STM32 notes (E68) meet in the fail-safe dual path with heartbeat plus interrupt in the What is a Track Circuit (E74) with two-channel wiring in the How to wire e-stop (E76).

Gentle touch fits finger scale on power and in time once a unit slip is fixed. Plain words: a grain-of-sand touch makes a tiny spot at gentle pressure that still clears the chip by a whisper, full grip does not bottom out, and the warning fits inside human reflex on spoon-light power. The numbers that decide it are 0.470 mm spot at 5.78 kPa in the Hertz contact radius (E14) on 0.269 pF base in the base capacitance gap (E26) giving 3.57 fF change in the check deltaC (E55) which corrects 0.00357 fF in the delta capacitance calculation (E28) as a unit slip, giving 14.6 Least Significant Bit, where Least Significant Bit means LSB, steps in the signal margin counts (E62), spanning to 213 kPa at 50 N in the dual-range sweep (E64), with 20.0 mm by 22.0 mm size inside 26 by 20 by 25 mm precedent in the BioTac Product Manual (E43) and 18.0 mm by 28.0 mm finger in the Free and Forced Vibration Modes (E60), 14.0 g mass in the mass budget sum (E53) about one-and-a-half teaspoons, 0.0991 W power in the power budget sum (E51) about one-tenth of a small lamp, 51.2 kbit per s rate in the SPI rate (E52), and 30.0 ms window inside 43.2 ms gap in the slip gap calculation (E84) from 53.6 ms to 96.8 ms in the stick-to-slip simulation (E38) needing 96.8 thousand multiply-accumulate, where multiply-accumulate means MAC, per s in the FIR rate (E78) for the 44-tap Finite Impulse Response, where Finite Impulse Response means FIR, filter, all everyday finger, blink and hum scales.

No blocking objection is open and each not ready vote is answered by this version plus named hardware proof. Plain words: thin stack keeps pressure, dual films keep slow and fast separate, facet drape keeps tiles flat, and fail-safe interrupt beats the slow frame, leaving only timed hardware to prove. The numbers that decide it are zero blocking objections on the board with 2200 Hz sampling and 30.0 ms window from the BioTac slip chapter (E31) fitting the 43.2 ms gap above, so Dr. Amara Okafor is answered by under 2.50 mm stack, Prof. Kenji Tanaka is answered by 14.6 steps margin plus no saturation, Dr. Elena Vasquez is answered by direct PVDF to MCU bypassing CDC for 100 to 500 Hz shake, and Dr. Marcus Reid is answered by 96.8 thousand MAC per s load plus flex continuity, with rub-cycle tear, shake-plus-pull continuity and timed slip-loop closure as bench tests, not open points.

RECORD: Decided F1 molded Shore A 10 dome plus ridges plus sipes, F2 nail-backed faceted core with M2 plus dovetail, F3 capacitive plus PVDF, F4 2.00 mm pitch centroid to 1 mm, F5 100 to 500 Hz power plus shear check in 30 ms, F6 fail-safe heartbeat plus interrupt plus SPI; numbers that stand are 0.470 mm at 5.78 kPa (E14), 0.269 pF base (E26), 3.57 fF change (E55 corrects E28), 14.6 LSB (E62), to 213 kPa (E64), 43.2 ms gap (E84) with 30 ms window (E38), 14.0 g (E53), 0.0991 W (E51), 51.2 kbit per s (E52), 20.0 by 22.0 mm (E43 E60); still open are member votes on proposal v1 and three bench tests, no blocking objection open. My position: not ready, because the members have not yet voted on proposal v1 and the timed hardware proof is still owed.
Note on Dr. Amara Okafor: set thin soft stack and ridge rules that let light touch through.
Note on Prof. Kenji Tanaka: gave taxel geometry and corrected signal margin without saturation.
Note on Dr. Elena Vasquez: set fast vibration path and timing gap that the message must beat.
Note on Dr. Marcus Reid: gave mount plus on-finger computer with fail-safe message that closes the loop.
